validity.researcher_notes: Neither figure matches the sheet. The three numbers may describe different measures, such as design, current and maximum capacity.

Length and diameter are backed by two documents. Operator is the Kazakh company only. Owner and start year have no citation. A May 2023 report says QazaqGaz launched a second line, which may need a new row.

fills.researcher_notes: A table of main gas pipelines from a Ukrainian gas transmission operator lists the Makat to North Caucasus trunk in two parts, 896 km and 48 km, which add up to the sheet value of 944 km. The table was read as a 2022 Wayback capture.

verifications.note: Government document lists the same diameters.

fills.researcher_notes: The table of main gas pipelines and a November 2020 Kazakhstan government document both give diameters of 1200, 1400 and 1420 mm for the trunk, which match the sheet list. The two documents have different origins.

verifications.note: Company page says it operates the main gas pipeline system in Kazakhstan, including Makat-North Caucasus.

fills.researcher_notes: The Intergas Central Asia company page says the company operates the Kazakh part of the Makat to North Caucasus gas pipeline. The sheet has no operator, so this fills it. The page covers the Kazakh section only, and the Russian section is operated by another company. A person may want to confirm that one operator fits the row.

No harvested citation states who owns the trunk. The sheet lists Gazprom PJSC and QazaqGaz. The Intergas page says its parent group is QazaqGaz, which fits the Kazakh part, but it does not say Gazprom owns anything. The Intergas Central Asia company may be a better owner for the Kazakh part. The sheet values stay. Not searched beyond the wiki citations this pass.

The sheet has 28.03 bcm per year. A Russian energy portal gives 21.9 bcm per year for the trunk. The 2020 Kazakhstan government document gives a maximum of 42.0 bcm per year. No citation gives 28.03. The sheet value stays and the conflict is filed as a concern.
The sources say the trunk was built in the 1980s but none states 1987. The sheet value stays and no reference was found. Not searched beyond the wiki citations this pass.

verifications.note: Report on launch of the second line.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Reports from May 2023 say QazaqGaz launched a second line of the Makat to North Caucasus gas pipeline after problems with the single line, which shows the trunk is in service.
